title: Five knots and the pinning theorem
claim: The 34 three-place knot relations form exactly five classes under flips and permutations: parity, Fibonacci (no-lone), not-all-equal, x or (y != z), clause. Only not-all-equal excludes both constant colourings, so on plain cubic systems it is the only knot that can fail; only the four signed not-all-equal relations are unchanged by flipping every colour, and such laws cannot pin a value. Pinning theorem: a signed law with a pinning piece, a relation that becomes an equality or disequality when one point is pinned, and a full piece is as hard on simple cubic systems as with unbounded occurrences (copy chains through pinned points, spare incidences absorbed by full pieces); with Schaefer this makes every non-affine such law NP-complete on cubic systems. Only parity is Schaefer-tractable. The clause cannot pin (a pinning piece would give an unsatisfiable cubic clause system, against Tovey). Checked: the generic reduction on 60 Fibonacci instances; Tovey on 300 random cubic clause systems; no pinning piece for the clause or not-all-equal with up to four internal points.
failure_conditions: A sixth class of three-place knots, or a knot other than not-all-equal excluding both constants.
A reduction instance whose cubic system differs in solvability from the source, or is not cubic or not simple.
A pinning piece for the clause or for not-all-equal.
foundation_claim_scope: A structural classification of the three-place knots and a gadget theorem for cubic systems; no counting claim.
